correctness.rationale: Direct algebra establishes x(1-x) f'(x)=f(x)(1-f(x))+(f(x)-x)^2 for each smooth constant-probability branch, all images remain interior, and log-odds conjugacy gives the exact nonnegative displacement-squared multiplicative correction. Telescoping conjugacy derivatives over any smooth closed orbit proves multiplier >1 for nonconstant cycles of every prime period. The quantitative bound uses f(x)(1-f(x)) <=1/4 and nonnegative products. Exact two-cycle (1/5,17/50), parameters (15/16,211/1122,1/2), gives multiplier 27389/22440. Cut points and endpoints explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: A cited primary theorem explicitly constructs oscillatory periodic population states, yet their stability across all periods is left undetermined. A single exact cocycle rules out all smooth attracting nonfixed cycles for unrestricted three-cell parameters, including branches with local ordinary derivatives as low as 1/2. The period-uniform lower bound is quantitative and directly relevant to which recurrent population configurations can be asymptotically stable. Not an arbitrary slice or known finite table.
